body: The report was simple: after picking individual files from a torrent, the bot's size-limit check cancelled downloads it should have allowed. The limit logic compared the wrong number.

In bot/modules/file_selector.py, the confirm_selection handler had two branches — one for aria2, one for qBittorrent. The aria2 branch correctly summed the sizes of just the selected files. The qBittorrent branch, however, assigned the torrent's total size to listener.size, ignoring the user's selection entirely. Pick 200 MB out of a 5 GB torrent and the bot still enforced the limit against 5 GB.

The fix mirrors the aria2 branch: sum only files whose priority is non-zero (the selected ones) and assign that to listener.size. A follow-up review from automated reviewers caught a second overwrite — _size_check in qbit_listener.py replaced the corrected size with tor.size whenever the torrent resumed — so that path now preserves the selected-files size too.
Small bug, real consequence: users with strict size limits couldn't download partial selections at all. The kind of thing you only find by reading both branches side by side.
items.summary: After file selection, the qBittorrent branch set the task size to the whole torrent instead of the selected files — so size limits cancelled downloads they shouldn't have.
items.title: The torrent size that lied

body: Some flags don't get deprecated. They just get deleted — and their tests get left behind.

The mirror-leech bot once had a -bh CLI flag for selecting BuzzHeavier as an upload destination. Commit 5f95760 retired the flag entirely: BuzzHeavier is now chosen through the upload destination option (-up bh). But two tests in tests/test_arg_parser_flags.py still asserted the old -bh behavior, and both were failing.

A codebase-wide search confirmed -bh survived nowhere else — not in the parser, not in the docs, not in any other test. The fix was pure deletion: remove the two stale tests and the last -bh references, and the suite is green again.

The lesson is a process one. When you remove a feature, grep for its ghost. Tests that assert deleted behavior don't just fail — they erode trust in the whole suite, because a red build everyone ignores hides the next real regression.
items.summary: The -bh flag was retired, but two arg-parser tests still asserted its behavior and failed. Removed the stale tests; suite green again.
items.title: The flag that retired quietly

body: Project-Deep-Focus fingerprints web servers from their headers. A FingerprintRule with a non-capturing pattern was wiping the version it had just detected — but only sometimes.

The bug was in FingerprintRule.evaluate(): on a non-capturing match it unconditionally overwrote last_groups with an empty tuple. Any version extracted from an earlier capturing group was discarded. Reproduction was crisp: with a Server header present the detected version came back None; without it, the same rule correctly returned 2.4.52.

The fix stops evaluate() from clobbering last_groups when the match captures nothing, and a regression test locks the behavior in — it fails on the old code and passes on the new. Full suite: 37 passed.

This is the classic stateful-parser bug: mutable state shared across evaluations, mutated on a code path nobody re-examined. The reproduction — same input, one header toggled — is what made it undeniable.
items.summary: FingerprintRule.evaluate() overwrote its captured groups on non-capturing matches, silently wiping the detected version. Fixed with a regression test.
items.title: The fingerprint that forgot its version

body: The unzip bot splits large archives into parts, sends them, and is supposed to clean up its _temp working file. It wasn't — at either call site.

The issue (upstream #375) was straightforward: after the split parts were delivered, the temporary file lingered on disk. On a busy bot that adds up fast. Both call sites that send split parts were missing the cleanup step.
The fix adds the _temp deletion after sending at both locations. Small diff, immediate effect: no more orphaned temp files accumulating between runs.
Not every bug is a puzzle. Some are just hygiene — and hygiene bugs in long-running bots become disk-space incidents. This one was reported by a user, fixed the same day, and merged.
items.summary: The bot left its _temp file behind after sending split archive parts. Added cleanup at both call sites — my first merged upstream contribution.
items.title: The temp file that overstayed
